summary: Part 1 of the Planet Labs deep dive (published 2026-09-19) answers investor questions about the recent stock-price decline. The quarter itself was strong: $116 million revenue, up 58% YoY, partly because a product for a customer was delivered earlier than expected (revenue pulled forward from next quarter). Highlights include commissioning and handover of the first sovereign Earth-observation satellite for the Swedish armed forces, a next-generation Pelican tech demo launch, and shipping two Tanager 1 and 18 SuperDove satellites. Defense and intelligence was the strongest category with 90% YoY revenue growth, and Europe/Middle East/Africa generated the most regional growth — no coincidence given Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts. Two post-quarter contract wins were announced: an $8 million deal with NGI and a smaller seven-figure contract. The company's deep archive of Earth imagery combined with AI pattern recognition provides 'indication and warning' capability for emerging threats. He argues degalization/decoupling trends will drive more conflict and therefore more demand for Planet's imagery. Note: captions garbled in places. Call: PL UNCERTAIN.
